execution.dry_runs_before_outcome_read: two dry runs on jaaks.synthetic_release (fake ticket, synthetic file, outputs in the session scratchpad, not in the repository); no Jaaks outcome was read by them
execution.code_changes_after_outcome_read: none to replay.py or test_allocation.py; posthoc.py and plan_addendum_1.json were added afterwards and read only written outputs
execution.test_changes_before_outcome_read: test_terminal_round_verifies_final_round_hits_when_reserve_suffices first asserted a terminal round in a degenerate all-hits case where verification consumed every round's capacity; the expectation (not the code) was wrong and was corrected before the real run

deviations.what: Field 'qc_excluded_replicate_plates' (planned as a lower bound on replicate plates failing QC) does not measure QC in this release.
deviations.evidence: build report: qc_rmse_excluded 0, missing_excluded 0, nan_rmse_rows 0 in 296,707 rows; the differences (0.5-1.5 plates per arm) come from the builder counting plates per anchor concentration and taking the maximum, while design plates count barcodes over both concentrations (763 of 148,735 orientation-plates hold one anchor concentration).
deviations.consequence: Failures of purchased measurements are 0 at orientation and exported-row level for every arm. Plates or curves rejected by the authors before export (Z-factor, CV, fit failures) are invisible and remain unknown. Reported under that interpretation; code unchanged.

deviations.what: In the physical version the fixed-split grid point f = 0.00 confirms 0.5 discoveries (not 0).
deviations.evidence: with costs of 14 x plates, screening cannot always exhaust W; the prespecified verification-first terminal round then spends the leftover wells on a verification when one fits.
deviations.consequence: f = 0 is not exactly screen-only in the physical version; immaterial for selection (chosen f 0.25-0.30).

deviations.what: Physical paired arms leave larger unavoidable remainders (1,315 wells static, 1,392 feedback, summed over 125 lines) than the other physical arms (370-440).
deviations.evidence: a pair costs >= 28 wells, so up to 27 wells per line-replicate cannot be used; every remainder was classed unavoidable by the prespecified rule (smaller than the cheapest still-available action), none avoidable.
deviations.consequence: static paired spends 80,192 combination wells against 81,130 for verify_hits_terminal (1.2% fewer) in the physical version; disclosed, not normalised away.

deviations.what: Interpretation of the round-R reserve rule.
deviations.evidence: plan.json says candidates are accepted 'only while' screen cost + ceil(reserve) fits; the code (fixed before the outcome read) skips a candidate whose acceptance would break the reserve and tries the next, consistent with the plan's general feasibility rule.
deviations.consequence: with unit costs the two readings differ only when a later candidate has a smaller p_s that avoids a ceil step; frequency not measured.

deviations.what: Brief item 5 asked for history = other lines of the same tissue; implemented as other lines of the same panel (same tissue AND same swap replicate).
deviations.evidence: this keeps the screen orientation of the history identical to the target's; P(validation) comes from the other orientation measured in other lines.
deviations.consequence: conf_per_cost uses other lines' validation-orientation calls, which no other arm uses: its contrast mixes predictor information and scheduling (see review note R1).

deviations.what: The custom-plate model treats each line x swap replicate as its own hypothetical campaign and averages SV and VS.
deviations.evidence: the same averaging as the discovery endpoint; physically a lab would run one of the two designs, not both.
deviations.consequence: plate counts are means of two hypothetical designs per line.

deviations.what: Native-plate model credits nothing for co-measured orientations and charges a native plate once (first touch).
deviations.evidence: a later purchase whose native plate was already run in an earlier round adds no plate, although in reality its result would have existed since that earlier round.
deviations.consequence: native plate counts are a lower bound for per-pair purchasing and the replay does not exploit plates already run; per-pair purchases are not physically separable in the native layout (only 5.9-10.8% of the combination wells on touched native plates belong to purchased orientations).

deviations.what: Post hoc additions after the outcome read.
deviations.evidence: plan_addendum_1.json: four time-matched contrasts (T1-T4) and summary tables computed from the written outputs only.
deviations.consequence: labelled POST HOC in results/posthoc_time_matched.json and results/summary_tables.json.

deviations.evidence: one record per line x replicate x non-random arm x version with every purchase
deviations.consequence: kept for audit; random-seed campaigns are summarised only.

review_notes.note: conf_per_cost beat verify_hits_terminal (268.0 vs 252.5 measurement; 265.5 vs 251.5 physical) but uses information the other static arms do not (historical validation-orientation calls of other lines). Its advantage is a predictor-plus-scheduler result, not a pure scheduling result.

Matching combination wells does not match plates or total wells: under the custom model with branch-separate plates, verify_hits_terminal uses 1,484 plates against 927 for screen-only and 1,293.5 for the fixed split (joint packing: 1,114.5, 927, 1,136.5). No plate-budget replay was prespecified or run.

Static paired (214.5) and static fixed split (231.5) reach the same outcomes in 1 and 2 rounds (R1 variants identical), whereas verify-hits needs 5 rounds for 252.5 and gets 210.5 in 2 rounds and 246.5 in 3.
